simple-interest.why: Simple interest pays only on the original amount: ~I = Prt~. It is rare in practice but it is the base case that makes compound interest understandable by contrast, and the formula rearranges to answer any of the four questions.
traps: The rate and the time must use the same period. A 6% annual rate over 18 months is t = 1.5, not 18.

compound-interest-intro.why: Compound interest pays on interest already earned, so growth is multiplicative: ~A = P(1+\f{r}{n})^{nt}~. This single formula explains savings, loans, inflation and why debt gets away from people. It is also where exponential functions first earn their keep.
traps: Divide the annual rate by the number of periods and multiply the years by the same number. Monthly at 12% means 1% twelve times a year, which is more than 12% a year.

code.note: Compare with simple interest, 1000 + 1000*0.12*5 = 1600. The gap is interest on interest.

percent-finance-words.why: Commission, margin, markup, unit price and loan payments are all percentage arithmetic with different vocabulary. The skill is identifying which quantity is the base — the number the percentage is *of* — because the words rarely say so outright.
traps: Markup is a percentage of cost; margin is a percentage of selling price. The same profit gives two different percentages, and quoting the flattering one is a standard sales tactic.
